assessments.reasoning: The dated W3C Recommendation defines named-instruction focus propagation in §10.1 and the template declaration override in §10.1.1. An omitted declaration permits the present focus to reach the constructor. A valid explicit absent declaration suppresses it for the callee constructor and callee parameters, even for a present caller. The distinction survives the dual name/match case because named invocation resolves by name. §9.10 separately governs caller-side supplied values. All seven cited ranges matched the independently fetched governing edition. The linked W3C errata index exposed no correction to those rules.

challenge.method: Independently apply the dated §§5.3.3.1, 6.2, 9.2.1, 9.10, 10.1 and 10.1.1 rules to a present non-singleton caller focus. Vary omitted declaration, valid absent declaration, caller-supplied argument, dual name/match, invalid absent/as, other use values and absent-versus-empty.
challenge.results: The omitted case inherited item, position and size. The valid absent case removed all three for callee evaluation, while an xsl:with-param expression retained the invocation focus. The dual name/match case did not alter these named-call outcomes. Invalid declarations, pattern dispatch, entry-point invocation and other use values remain outside the claim.

limitations: Only the 8 June 2017 XSLT 3.0 Recommendation and the two stated valid named-call branches were assessed.

The focus is the initial evaluation context of the callee constructor and callee parameter evaluation. Supplied caller-side argument expressions, unused defaults, later focus changes within instructions, and focus-dependent evaluation errors have separate rules.
The challenge directly evaluated the normative rules. No stylesheet processor was run and no implementation behavior was measured.
Independent Codex execution verified the same governing source. The execution does not supply a second normative authority.
